newsitem.title: UK: Harry Ramsden's serves up profits rise.
newsitem.headline: Harry Ramsden's serves up profits rise.

text.p: British fish and chip chain Harry Ramsden's Plc dished up a healthy 16 percent rise in annual profits and unwapped plans on Thursday to open another seven restaurants during 1997.
The chain, started by namesake Harry Ramsden in 1928, announced that pretax profit increased to 1.34 million pounds in the year to September 29, 1996 from 1.15 million previously.

"This progress reflected continued brand building through increasing the number of restaurants and franchise partners and extending the successful brand licensing business," the company said in its results statement.
It said it would be paying an unchanged dividend of four pence per share making a total of five pence for the year.

Harry Ramsden's, which currently has 21 restaurants, including one in Australia and another in Hong Kong, plans to open seven more in 1997 from Singapore and Saudia Arabia to Inverness in Scotland and Southampton in England.
Turnover at the company rose 13 percent during the year to stand at 4.89 million pounds.
The company opened its first franchised counter service in Tenerife, Spain, in the summer followed by a second counter service with Compass Group Plc in Glasgow airport in Scotland in January.

Elsewhere in the group, Harry Ramsden's said its brand licensing business grew strongly due primarily to the success of the oven bake range of Harry Ramsden's approved Ross/Young's fish and chip products.
